detail.title: Thermodynamics and Temporal Correlations in Information Engines
detail.summary: Memory functions as a bridge between past environmental correlations and future work, not merely as a storage register. By utilizing evidence from automata learning and real-time systems, we establish that 'memory' in an operational sense requires the system to maintain distinct causal states capable of regulating output in response to input sequences, rather than simple state retention. The thermodynamic cost of this maintenance is fundamentally linked to the entropy rate of the input process and the precision of the predictive model.
detail.reason: Revising to integrate new evidence on state-merging and real-time scheduling constraints.
